comments.body:
PHASE 1 / STAGE 1 — DESCRIPTIVE DOSSIER (no root-cause claim yet)

Report: another session manually cleared GitHub Actions runs that appeared stuck. Authenticated GitHub inspection on 2026-07-31/08-01 found five Gerrit Verified Gate runs cancelled together around 00:15Z: 30659951798 (change 1129/PS2, started 19:39Z), 30661386050 (1131/PS1, 20:02Z), 30668540449 (1130/PS4, 22:00Z), 30668541953 (1131/PS2, 22:00Z), and 30668543617 (1136/PS2, 22:00Z). URLs: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/30659951798, /30661386050, /30668540449, /30668541953, /30668543617.

Observed job state: these were not queued for runners. Every affected run assigned GitHub-hosted runners; lint, packaging, ticket, identity, and other jobs completed. All four pytest matrix cells (Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13) entered the default suite, advanced to the 99% progress line in roughly 6–18 minutes, then emitted nothing for 1.7–4.3 hours until manual cancellation. The active step on every cancelled matrix job was `Run the default suite (Python tiers; excludes integration + external)`.

Recheck state: the clearing session dispatched the same exact stale patchsets again at 00:14Z (runs 30675030213=1129/PS2, 30675031552=1130/PS4, 30675032723=1131/PS2, 30675034104=1136/PS2). Those rechecks were still in_progress when gathered; a later run was queued behind them. No cancellation/rerun/dispatch was performed by this investigation.

Git ancestry: 1129/PS2 -> 1130/PS4 -> 1131/PS2 -> 1136/PS2 form a stacked feature history; 1131/PS1 is an earlier revision of the same stack. All five affected revisions diverge from current main at fde6baae and OMIT merged commit 96a0d5c3f (`747f: fetch blobs in one RPC before materializing`). A contemporaneous independent change, run 30668764517 (1140/PS1), includes 747f in its ancestry and all four matrix jobs completed successfully (Ubuntu ~6–8m, macOS ~17m).

Prior incident evidence: closed bug 747f-d1ba-dd43-43f4 is titled `materialize/_materialize_tree can lazy-fetch unboundedly on a partial clone ... hang for hours`. Its certified fix commit 96a0d5c3f records the measured mechanism: blobless fetch + read-tree without -u + checkout-index bypasses git batch prefetch, causing one sequential fetch RPC per missing blob; about 25,561 ticket-tree files projected to ~2.1h. It adds one bounded unfiltered blob refill and git timeouts. Closed ticket 72d9 comment records earlier faulthandler proof of the CI-lane hang through `attested resolve -> materialize_tickets -> git checkout-index lazy-fetching on CI shallow+blobless clone`.

Workflow evidence: `.github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml` correctly checks out the exact Gerrit refspec. `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml` runs the default suite under xdist but declares no `timeout-minutes` at the job or step, so a recurrence remains in-progress until GitHub default limits or manual cancellation.

Open questions / leads to test (not conclusions):
1. Leading: affected patchsets repeat the already-proven 747f per-blob lazy-fetch mechanism because their stale stack omits 96a0d5c3f. Discriminate with the 747f blob-starved fixture or git trace against affected vs fixed trees.
2. Alternative: a new test in change 1129 independently hangs at 99%; discriminate by running the final test selection with/without the 1129 diff while holding the 747f fix constant.
3. Alternative: hosted runner capacity/platform outage; runner assignment on every job and cross-platform simultaneous 99% freeze weigh against it, but compare a contemporaneous fixed-ancestry run.
4. Separate resilience question: absence of a repository-level timeout explains why confirmed hangs require manual clearing, but defect legitimacy and the correct bound still need an authoritative contract/caller sweep before repair.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
PHASE 1 COMPLETE — confirmed parsimonious account and experiments

Primary defect (already repaired on main, still present in stale Gerrit patchsets): affected 1129/1130/1131/1136 revisions omit 96a0d5c3f and retain unconditional --filter=blob:none followed by read-tree + checkout-index with no up-front blob refill. Exact 1129 code failed the blob-starved no-lazy-fetch oracle with all 40 blobs absent; the same tree with 96a0d5c3f passed. A GIT_TRACE2_EVENT runtime probe on pre-fix code observed 40 git-fetch child starts for 40 files; fixed main passed both the completeness and bounded-fetch oracles. The base fde6 run 30660757264 froze before 1129 tests existed; isolated 1129 tests passed in 1.66s. Runner outage and merely-slow-suite alternatives are rejected. Closed bug 747f and its certified regression contract establish defect legitimacy.

Containment defect: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml test job has no timeout-minutes, so GitHub applies its 360-minute default. The rerun burst occupied 16 matrix jobs while later run 30676012105 queued, explaining why manual cancellation clears the queue. The workflow documents normal 10–16 minute execution; a 60-minute job bound preserves a >3x macOS margin while eliminating manual-clear dependence. Empirical evidence resolves the code-tracer/historical legitimacy ambiguity in favor of defect.

Caller/dependency sweep: _build-and-test.yml has exactly two callers, test.yml and gerrit-verify.yaml. Both consume the same test job result and benefit from a bounded failure; neither behaviorally depends on six-hour execution. Expected post-fix behavior: every reusable pytest matrix job ends success/failure within 60 minutes, and a blocked worker cannot retain a hosted slot beyond that bound.

PHASE 2 TEST CONTRACT CARD
authoritative_contract: user incident requirement that CI not remain manual-clear-dependent; _build-and-test.yml documents 10–16m normal duration; GitHub workflow syntax defines timeout-minutes as the job execution bound and defaults omission to 360m.
trigger_preconditions: reusable workflow test job exists and runs the OS/Python matrix.
production_path: parsed .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml jobs.test configuration consumed by both CI callers.
test_tier: config-as-artifact unit test; a lower tier cannot validate workflow configuration, and live dispatch is intentionally not authorized.
observable_postcondition: jobs.test.timeout-minutes is exactly 60.
ci_gate: default pytest suite / make test.
negative_control: omitted — single-point configuration defect.
gating proof to capture: exact node collected, executed, RED before workflow edit.

comments.body: HISTORICAL PERFORMANCE CHECK — do not move the blocker to integration. Examined 12 successful GitHub Actions pytest cells across runs 30668764517, 30669480919, and 30670941755 (three Ubuntu Python versions plus macOS). After the 99% progress line, the entire remaining default-suite tail completed in 7.9–34.8s; Linux tails were 17.3–29.5s. Whole default suites completed in 4m18s–6m22s on Linux and 8m21s–14m45s on macOS. The materialization-triggering item was absent from every slowest-25 report, so its phase duration was below each cell cutoff: 2.40–3.61s on Linux and 2.49–4.85s on macOS. Even the slowest listed default-suite phase was only 16.03s Linux / 35.06s macOS. Therefore there is no evidence of normal runtime above one minute; the hours-long behavior is the confirmed per-blob lazy-fetch defect, not legitimate test cost. Moving the item would hide a fast default-suite regression and would not address the mechanism.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
Recent GitHub Actions runs have remained stuck until another session manually cleared them. Use the repository `rebar-debug` protocol to prove the recurring mechanism and repair every confirmed defect in scope. Do not mutate live GitHub run state during investigation.

## Plan
### Phase 1 — Understand
- Gather a descriptive dossier from authenticated Actions run/job metadata, timestamps, cancellation history, workflow definitions, repository settings, ticket/history evidence, and recent relevant changes.
- Treat this as a chronic incident unless evidence disproves recurrence; generate falsifiable competing hypotheses through the skill-required independent investigation step.
- Run read-only discriminating experiments and require runtime/API evidence of the mechanism before declaring a root cause. Establish defect legitimacy against repository workflow contracts or prior fixed behavior, then sweep callers/dependencies of the artifact proposed for change.

### Phase 2 — Repair (only after Phase 1 proves a defect)
- Read the skill test-design standard, inventory coverage, and create the smallest regression oracle that exercises the proven mechanism. Observe it RED for the expected reason before editing production workflow/code.
- Implement the mechanism-level fix while the RED oracle is held out from the fixer, then restore it and prove GREEN. Seed the exact defect as a mutation and confirm the oracle returns RED before restoring the fix.
- Run relevant workflow validation, lint/tests, and replicate the original stuck-run scenario through a local or read-only-safe equivalent. Sweep for confirmed siblings of the same pattern.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The affected run pattern is identified with URLs and timestamps, checked via `gh run list` and Actions API metadata.
- [ ] A parsimonious root cause is confirmed by discriminating evidence that explains why manual clearing unsticks the queue and rejects competing runner-capacity, concurrency, workflow, and platform hypotheses.
- [ ] Defect legitimacy and the bounded caller/dependency sweep are documented before any production edit.
- [ ] Each confirmed defect has a regression oracle observed RED before the fix, GREEN after it, and RED again under a defect-seeded mutation.
- [ ] Relevant `make lint`, targeted tests, Actions workflow validation, and a safe replication of the original scenario pass after the fix.
- [ ] Findings, experiments, decisions, and final verification are recorded in `rebar comment` updates on this ticket.

## Verification
Use read-only `gh run list`, `gh run view`, and `gh api` queries; inspect `.github/workflows/` and relevant history; then run the exact targeted tests introduced for the confirmed mechanism plus `make lint` and the repository workflow validators. No live run cancellation, rerun, dispatch, or repository-setting change is authorized.
